# ds-pstack
**把 pstack 的 58 个严谨工程 skill 搬到 DeepSeek Harness，子 agent 的模型自动从你勾选的模型里挑，分类不另打一次模型。**
Lauren Tan's pstack agent workflows, ported to DeepSeek Harness. Same 58 skills, plus a deterministi
c router that picks each subagent's model from the models *you* checked.

pstack for DeepSeek Harness. pstack is Lauren Tan's set of agent workflows: write less code, but hig
her quality code, and parallelize with confidence.
This port keeps pstack's playbooks, principles, and prose rules. Two things change, because DeepSeek
Harness works differently from Cursor.
**The skills are the same skills.** All 58 of them, in the `/` menu under their pstack names. `/pote
to-mode` runs the playbook, `/interrogate` runs the adversarial review, `/how` explains a subsystem,
and the 24 `principle-*` skills carry the reasoning pstack is built on.
**The models are chosen for you, out of your own list.** pstack on Cursor names a model slug per rol
e. ds-pstack cannot do that, because a Harness profile's models are whatever you configured and chec
ked. So the router reads the child's task, decides what kind of work it is, and picks the best route
from the models you checked for subagents. A skill never names a model. The router picks from that
checked pool, and `/setup-pstack` is the only place a route is pinned.
## Install
The package installs as a Harness bundle, straight from this repository:

That adds two plugin rows to the profile. Disable either one to keep the other.
| Row | What it does when disabled |

| `ds-pstack-skills` | pstack's skills leave the catalog; routing still works |
| `ds-pstack-router`
| every child runs on the route it inherited; skills still work |
### Updates
Installing from the repository means updates are a pull, not a reinstall. The profile records a git
dependency, so the next fetch picks up whatever is on `main`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The profile's package manager resolves the branch to a commit and records both. Skill text reloads f
rom disk on its own. The router's JavaScript is a separate module generation, so after an update tha
t changes `lib/` the plugin has to be re-mounted: toggle the `ds-pstack-router` row off and on in Pl
ugin Manager, which re-imports the module. A full app restart also works, and is the simpler option
h re-imports the module. A full app restart also works, and is the simpler option if you are unsure.
To develop against a checkout instead of the published copy, install it by path (`plugin_manager ins
tall_bundle /absolute/path`) and reinstall from the git spec when you are done.
To stay on a fixed release instead of tracking `main`, install a tag:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
A tag pins that commit until you install again. New tags are published as `v<version>` when the vers
ion in `package.json` changes.
## The model pool is yours
ds-pstack chooses only from the routes checked in **Settings → Subagent model selection** (`subagent
-model-selection-settings.allowedModels`). That setting is the authorization boundary, so the router
never widens it: the route it selects is always one you checked, even when another model would suit
the route it selects is always one you checked, even when another model would suit the task better.
Checking one model means each routed child runs on that model with a routing-chosen effort. Checking
several means the router can match a cheap fast model to mechanical work and a strong one to review
. With none checked, the router leaves each child on the route it inherited. A forked child keeps it
s inherited route unless `routeForkedChildren` is turned on, and a delegation that already names `pr
ovider`, `model`, or `reasoning_effort` is left alone.
To check models, open Settings, find Subagent model selection, enable it, and select the routes you
, open Settings, find Subagent model selection, enable it, and select the routes you want available.
## How a child's route is chosen
Every delegated child makes a model request. Before the first one, the router:

1. reads the delegation prompt, which is the brief the parent wrote;
2. classifies the work into one
of eight intents (`planning`, `coding`, `debugging`, `review`, `research`, `analysis`, `writing`, `

mechanical`) and reads its difficulty;
3. picks an effort from your pstack budget, that intent, and
onto one the chosen route actually advertises.

### Budgets
pstack's four budget labels still apply. `/setup-pstack` writes the one you choose:
| Budget | Base effort | Effect |
[该节后续省略]
## What did not port
Cursor-only machinery: Automations, the Bugbot feed, cloud agents, and `-fast` speed selection. Wher
e a playbook step needs one, the skill says so in one line and continues. The full mapping is in doc
s/harness/deepseek-harness.md.
